entries.title: Concurrent Chemotherapy and Radiotherapy for Organ Preservation in Advanced Laryngeal Cancer
entries.organization: Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (RTOG) / NRG Oncology
entries.stage_criteria: Stage III or IV nonmetastatic squamous cell carcinoma of glottic or supraglottic larynx requiring total laryngectomy (T2-T4, N0-N3, M0; excluding T1 and T4 with extensive cartilage invasion)

trial_arms.intervention: Definitive RT 70 Gy in 35 daily fractions (2.0 Gy/fx) with concurrent Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 22, and 43
Induction Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 + 5-FU 1000 mg/m2/day continuous infusion d1-5 x 3 cycles followed by definitive RT 70 Gy
Definitive RT 70 Gy in 35 daily fractions (2.0 Gy/fx)

key_passages.text: Concurrent cisplatin and radiotherapy provides superior locoregional control and larynx preservation compared with induction chemotherapy followed by radiation or radiation alone. Long-term overall survival did not differ significantly between arms.

Concurrent chemoradiotherapy was associated with a relative risk reduction of locoregional failure of 42% compared with RT alone (HR 0.58, p=0.0015) and 34% compared with induction chemotherapy (HR 0.66, p=0.0037).

entries.clinical_recommendation: Concurrent high-dose cisplatin (100 mg/m2 q3w) with definitive radiation (70 Gy) is the standard nonsurgical organ preservation strategy for locally advanced laryngeal cancer.

entries.title: Postoperative Concurrent Chemotherapy and Radiotherapy for High-Risk Squamous-Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck
entries.organization: European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC)
entries.stage_criteria: Resected stage III-IV squamous-cell carcinoma of oral cavity, oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx with high-risk features (positive surgical margins, extranodal extension, pT3-T4, vascular/perineural invasion, or level IV/V nodal involvement)

trial_arms.intervention: Postoperative RT 66 Gy in 33 fractions (2.0 Gy/fx) with concurrent Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 22, and 43
Postoperative RT 66 Gy in 33 fractions (2.0 Gy/fx)

key_passages.text: Postoperative concurrent administration of cisplatin with radiotherapy resulted in significant improvements in progression-free survival (HR 0.75, p=0.04), overall survival (HR 0.70, p=0.02), and locoregional control (HR 0.57, p=0.007) compared with radiotherapy alone in high-risk head and neck cancer.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Postoperative concurrent cisplatin (100 mg/m2 q3w x 3 cycles) plus 66 Gy radiation is standard for resected head and neck cancer with positive margins or extranodal nodal extension.

entries.title: Postoperative Concurrent Radiotherapy and Chemotherapy for High-Risk Squamous-Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck
entries.stage_criteria: Resected stage III-IV squamous-cell carcinoma of oral cavity, oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx with >=2 involved regional lymph nodes, extracapsular extension (ENE), or microscopically positive surgical margins

trial_arms.intervention: Postoperative RT 60-66 Gy in 30-33 fractions + concurrent Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 22, and 43
Postoperative RT 60-66 Gy in 30-33 fractions

key_passages.text: Concurrent postoperative radiotherapy and cisplatin significantly improved locoregional control (HR 0.61, p=0.01) and disease-free survival (HR 0.78, p=0.04) among high-risk patients with resected head and neck cancer.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Adjuvant cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy significantly reduces locoregional failure in surgically resected HNSCC harboring positive margins or extracapsular nodal spread.

entries.title: Defining Risk Levels in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Cancers: A Comparative Analysis of Concurrent Postoperative Radiation Plus Chemotherapy Trials of the EORTC (#22931) and RTOG (#9501)
entries.stage_criteria: Pooled patient-level data from 792 patients enrolled in EORTC 22931 and RTOG 9501

key_passages.text: Definitive benefit of postoperative concurrent cisplatin and RT is restricted to patients with microscopically positive surgical margins and/or extracapsular extension (ECE/ENE). Patients with multiple involved nodes without ECE did not demonstrate an overall survival benefit from adding chemotherapy.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Microscopically positive surgical margins and extranodal nodal extension are the absolute standard indications for adjuvant concurrent chemoradiation; patients with other intermediate features (T3-4, multiple nodes without ENE) may receive RT alone.

entries.title: Randomized Phase III Trial of Concurrent Accelerated Radiation Plus Cisplatin With or Without Cetuximab for Stage III to IV Head and Neck Carcinoma
entries.organization: Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (RTOG) / NRG Oncology
entries.stage_criteria: Nonmetastatic stage III/IV squamous cell carcinoma of oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx

trial_arms.intervention: Accelerated RT (72 Gy in 42 fractions over 6 weeks) + Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV d1, 22
Accelerated RT + Cisplatin + Cetuximab (400 mg/m2 loading, then 250 mg/m2 weekly)

endpoints.grade_3_4_adverse_events: Significantly higher mucositis and radiation dermatitis in cetuximab arm

key_passages.text: The addition of cetuximab to cisplatin-based concurrent accelerated radiation therapy failed to improve progression-free survival or overall survival and resulted in more frequent interruptions in radiation therapy and worse acute toxic effects. Cisplatin + RT remains standard.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Cetuximab should not be added to standard concurrent cisplatin-radiotherapy in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

entries.title: Radiotherapy with or without Cetuximab in the Treatment of Locoregionally Advanced Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck
entries.stage_criteria: Locoregionally advanced Stage III-IV squamous cell carcinoma of oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx

trial_arms.intervention: Definitive RT (70 Gy) + Cetuximab (400 mg/m2 load then 250 mg/m2 weekly)
Definitive RT alone (70 Gy)

key_passages.text: Definitive radiotherapy plus cetuximab significantly improves locoregional control and overall survival compared with radiotherapy alone in locoregionally advanced head and neck cancer, without exacerbating common radiation-related mucositis.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Cetuximab + definitive RT is a Category 1 alternative for patients with locally advanced HNSCC who are medically unfit for cisplatin (e.g. renal failure, pre-existing neuropathy, severe hearing loss).

entries.title: Radiotherapy plus Cetuximab or Cisplatin in Human Papillomavirus-Positive Oropharyngeal Cancer: A Randomised, Multicentre, Non-Inferiority Trial
entries.stage_criteria: Locally advanced HPV/p16-positive squamous cell carcinoma of oropharynx (T1-T2 N2a-N3 or T3-T4 N0-N3, AJCC 7th)

trial_arms.intervention: Accelerated IMRT 70 Gy in 35 fx / 6 wks + Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 d1, 22
Accelerated IMRT 70 Gy in 35 fx / 6 wks + Cetuximab loading and weekly

key_passages.text: For patients with HPV-positive oropharyngeal carcinoma, radiotherapy plus cetuximab showed inferior overall survival and progression-free survival compared with radiotherapy plus cisplatin, with similar rates of overall acute and late toxicity. Radiotherapy plus cisplatin remains the standard of care.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Cisplatin concurrent with definitive radiotherapy remains the non-negotiable standard of care for HPV-positive oropharynx cancer; cetuximab de-intensification is inferior and not guideline concordant.

entries.title: Durvalumab after Chemoradiotherapy in Stage III Non–Small-Cell Lung Cancer
entries.stage_criteria: Unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer with no progression after definitive concurrent platinum-based chemoradiotherapy (minimum RT dose 54-66 Gy)

trial_arms.intervention: Durvalumab 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks for up to 12 months
Placebo every 2 weeks for up to 12 months

key_passages.text: Consolidation durvalumab significantly prolonged progression-free survival and overall survival compared with placebo in patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC who did not have disease progression after concurrent chemoradiotherapy, with manageable safety profile.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Durvalumab consolidation (10 mg/kg q2w or 1500 mg q4w x 12 months) is Category 1 standard of care following definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy in non-progressing unresectable stage III NSCLC.

entries.title: High-Dose Radiotherapy with or without Cetuximab for Patients with Inoperable Stage III Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer: A Multicentre, Randomised, Open-Label Phase 3 Study
entries.organization: Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (RTOG) / NRG Oncology
entries.stage_criteria: Inoperable stage III non-small cell lung cancer, ECOG 0-1, FEV1 >= 1.2 L or >= 50% predicted

trial_arms.intervention: 60 Gy in 30 daily fractions + concurrent carboplatin/paclitaxel +/- cetuximab
74 Gy in 37 daily fractions + concurrent carboplatin/paclitaxel +/- cetuximab

endpoints.multivariate_predictors_of_death: High-dose radiation arm (HR 1.35) and heart V40/V5/V30 dose volume parameters

key_passages.text: 74 Gy radiation dose escalation was harmful compared with standard-dose 60 Gy thoracic radiotherapy in stage III NSCLC. Excess mortality was strongly correlated with cardiac radiation exposure. Standard 60 Gy in 30 fractions remains the definitive standard.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Definitive radiation prescription for stage III NSCLC must not exceed 60-66 Gy in standard 2 Gy fractions; strict cardiac sparing (mean heart dose, V30, V5) is essential.

entries.title: Concurrent Once-Daily versus Twice-Daily Chemoradiotherapy in Patients with Limited-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer
entries.organization: CONVERT Study Team / Cancer Research UK
entries.stage_criteria: Limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC), ECOG performance status 0-1, normal organ function

trial_arms.intervention: 45 Gy in 30 fractions (1.5 Gy bid over 3 weeks) + concurrent cisplatin/etoposide
66 Gy in 33 fractions (2.0 Gy qd over 6.5 weeks) + concurrent cisplatin/etoposide

key_passages.text: Survival outcomes and toxicity were similar between twice-daily 45 Gy and once-daily 66 Gy chemoradiotherapy. Twice-daily 45 Gy in 3 weeks remains the standard international benchmark, with once-daily 66 Gy offering a safe and valid alternative.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Accelerated twice-daily thoracic radiotherapy (45 Gy in 30 fx bid over 3 weeks) starting with Cycle 1-2 of cisplatin/etoposide is standard for limited-stage SCLC.

entries.title: Radiotherapy to the Primary Tumour for Newly Diagnosed, Metastatic Prostate Cancer (STAMPEDE): A Randomised Controlled Phase 3 Trial
entries.organization: MRC Clinical Trials Unit / STAMPEDE Investigators
entries.stage_criteria: Newly diagnosed metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC / mCSPC)

trial_arms.intervention: Lifelong ADT +/- early Docetaxel
Standard systemic therapy + Prostate RT (55 Gy / 20 fx daily over 4 weeks or 36 Gy / 6 fx weekly over 6 weeks)

key_passages.text: Prostate radiotherapy improved overall survival in men with newly diagnosed metastatic prostate cancer who had low metastatic burden (CHAARTED criteria: <4 bone metastases and no visceral metastases). Primary prostate RT should be recommended for low-volume mHSPC.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Prostate-directed external beam radiotherapy (55 Gy / 20 fx or 36 Gy / 6 fx) is standard Category 1 therapy for men with newly diagnosed low-volume metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer.

entries.title: Radiotherapy with or without Short-Term Androgen Deprivation for Localized Prostate Cancer
entries.stage_criteria: Localized adenocarcinoma of the prostate (T1b-T2b, PSA <= 20 ng/mL, Gleason score <= 7)

trial_arms.intervention: Definitive RT 66.6 Gy
Definitive RT 66.6 Gy + 4 months of ADT (Flutamide + Goserelin starting 2 months prior to RT)

endpoints.subgroup_benefit: Benefit concentrated entirely in intermediate-risk disease; low-risk patients showed no OS improvement (p=0.48)

key_passages.text: The addition of 4 months of short-term androgen-deprivation therapy to radiotherapy significantly improved overall survival and decreased disease-specific mortality for men with intermediate-risk localized prostate cancer.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Short-term androgen deprivation therapy (4 to 6 months) combined with definitive radiation therapy is Category 1 standard for intermediate-risk prostate cancer.

entries.title: Duration of Androgen Suppression in the Treatment of Locally Advanced Prostate Cancer
entries.organization: European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC)
entries.stage_criteria: Locally advanced / high-risk localized prostate cancer (T1c-T2b N0 with PSA >= 3x ULN or Gleason >= 8, or T3-T4 N0-N1)

trial_arms.intervention: External beam RT (70 Gy) + 6 months LHRH agonist
External beam RT (70 Gy) + 36 months LHRH agonist

key_passages.text: The combination of radiotherapy plus 6 months of androgen suppression provides inferior overall survival compared with radiotherapy plus 3 years of androgen suppression in locally advanced and high-risk prostate cancer.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Long-term androgen deprivation therapy (24-36 months) in combination with high-dose definitive radiotherapy is the established standard for high-risk and very high-risk localized prostate cancer.

entries.title: Radiotherapy with or without Chemotherapy in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer
entries.organization: BC2001 Trial Investigators / Cancer Research UK
entries.stage_criteria: Muscle-invasive adenocarcinoma or urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder (T2-T4a N0 M0)

trial_arms.intervention: Definitive pelvic RT (55 Gy / 20 fx or 64 Gy / 32 fx)
Definitive pelvic RT + 5-FU (500 mg/m2/d d1-5 & d16-20) + Mitomycin C (12 mg/m2 d1)

endpoints.salvage_cystectomy_rate: Significantly reduced with CRT without increased late toxic effects

key_passages.text: Synchronous chemotherapy with fluorouracil and mitomycin C during definitive radiotherapy significantly improved locoregional disease-free survival and reduced cystectomy rates without increasing late grade 3 or 4 adverse events.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Concurrent 5-FU and Mitomycin C with definitive radiotherapy is the Category 1 standard regimen for trimodality bladder-preserving therapy in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

entries.title: Preoperative Chemoradiotherapy for Esophageal or Junctional Cancer
entries.stage_criteria: Resectable esophageal or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, or large-cell carcinoma (cT1N1 or cT2-3N0-1, M0)

trial_arms.intervention: Transthoracic or transhiatal esophagectomy with lymphadenectomy
Weekly Paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 + Carboplatin AUC 2 for 5 weeks with concurrent RT 41.4 Gy (23 fx of 1.8 Gy) followed by surgery

key_passages.text: Preoperative chemoradiotherapy with weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel combined with 41.4 Gy radiation significantly improved overall survival compared with surgery alone in patients with resectable esophageal or GEJ cancer.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy using the CROSS regimen (weekly carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 with 41.4 Gy RT) is a standard Category 1 trimodality approach for resectable esophageal and GEJ cancers.

entries.title: Adjuvant Nivolumab in Resected Esophageal or Gastroesophageal Junction Cancer
entries.stage_criteria: Resected stage II or III esophageal or gastroesophageal junction cancer with residual pathologic disease (>= ypT1 or ypN+) after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and R0 surgical resection

trial_arms.intervention: Nivolumab 240 mg IV q2w for 16 weeks, then 480 mg q4w up to total 1 year
Placebo for up to total 1 year

key_passages.text: Among patients with resected esophageal or GE junction cancer who had received neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and had residual pathologic disease, disease-free survival was significantly doubled with adjuvant nivolumab compared with placebo.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Adjuvant Nivolumab for 1 year is Category 1 standard for patients with residual pathologic disease (non-pCR) following neoadjuvant chemoradiation and complete resection.

entries.title: Short-Course Radiotherapy Followed by Chemotherapy before Total Mesorectal Excision (TME) versus Preoperative Chemoradiotherapy, TME, and Optional Adjuvant Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (RAPIDO): A Randomised, Open-Label, Phase 3 Trial
entries.stage_criteria: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma with high-risk features on pelvic MRI: cT4a/b, extramural venous invasion (EMVI+), cN2, involved mesorectal fascia (MRF+), or enlarged lateral lymph nodes

trial_arms.intervention: Short-course RT (5 x 5 Gy = 25 Gy in 1 week) -> 6 cycles CAPOX or 9 cycles FOLFOX4 consolidation chemotherapy -> TME surgery
Long-course CRT (50-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fx + Capecitabine) -> TME surgery -> optional adjuvant CAPOX/FOLFOX

key_passages.text: Total neoadjuvant therapy with short-course radiotherapy followed by consolidation chemotherapy before TME significantly reduced the probability of disease-related treatment failure and distant metastasis and doubled the pathological complete response rate compared with standard chemoradiotherapy.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Total Neoadjuvant Therapy (TNT) using short-course RT (5x5 Gy) followed by consolidation CAPOX/FOLFOX is Category 1 standard for MRI-defined high-risk locally advanced rectal cancer.

entries.title: Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy with FOLFIRINOX and Preoperative Chemoradiotherapy for Patients with Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (UNICANCER-PRODIGE 23): A Multicentre, Randomised, Open-Label, Phase 3 Trial
entries.stage_criteria: Locally advanced rectal cancer (cT3 or cT4, M0)

trial_arms.intervention: 6 cycles mFOLFIRINOX induction -> Preoperative CRT (50 Gy + Capecitabine) -> TME surgery -> 3 months adjuvant mFOLFOX6
Preoperative CRT (50 Gy + Capecitabine) -> TME surgery -> 6 months adjuvant mFOLFOX6

key_passages.text: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with mFOLFIRINOX before preoperative chemoradiotherapy significantly improved disease-free survival, metastasis-free survival, and pathological complete response rate compared with standard preoperative chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Induction mFOLFIRINOX followed by preoperative chemoradiotherapy is a Category 1 TNT regimen for fit patients with locally advanced rectal cancer.

entries.title: Chemoradiation with or without Maintenance Chemotherapy for Anal Cancer (ACT II): A Randomised, Factorial, Phase 3 Trial
entries.organization: UK NCRI Anal Cancer Sub-Group / ACT II
entries.stage_criteria: Epidermoid anal canal carcinoma (any stage without distant metastasis)

trial_arms.intervention: RT 50.4 Gy + 5-FU 1000 mg/m2/d d1-4 & d29-32 + Mitomycin C 12 mg/m2 d1
RT 50.4 Gy + 5-FU 1000 mg/m2/d d1-4 & d29-32 + Cisplatin 60 mg/m2 d1, 29

endpoints.maintenance_chemotherapy_effect: No benefit in PFS (HR 0.95, p=0.70) or OS (HR 0.86, p=0.37); caused added toxicity

key_passages.text: Mitomycin C and Cisplatin produced equivalent response rates and progression-free survival, but Cisplatin caused higher hematologic toxicity. Maintenance chemotherapy provided no clinical benefit. 5-FU and Mitomycin C concurrent with radiotherapy remains the definitive standard of care.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Definitive chemoradiation with 5-FU and Mitomycin C is the standard of care for epidermoid anal cancer; maintenance chemotherapy should not be administered.

entries.title: FOLFIRINOX or Gemcitabine as Adjuvant Therapy for Pancreatic Cancer
entries.stage_criteria: Completely resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (R0 or R1 resection), ECOG performance status 0-1, postoperative CA19-9 < 180 U/mL

trial_arms.intervention: Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, Leucovorin 400 mg/m2, Irinotecan 180 or 150 mg/m2, 5-FU continuous 2400 mg/m2 over 46h q2w for 24 weeks (12 cycles)
Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, 15 q28d for 6 cycles

key_passages.text: Adjuvant therapy with a modified FOLFIRINOX regimen led to significantly longer overall survival and disease-free survival than gemcitabine among patients with resected pancreatic cancer.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Modified FOLFIRINOX is the Category 1 standard adjuvant chemotherapy for fit patients (ECOG 0-1, preserved organ function) following resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

entries.title: Cisplatin, Radiation, and Adjuvant Hysterectomy for Bulky Stage IB Cervical Carcinoma
entries.stage_criteria: Bulky stage IB carcinoma of the cervix (tumor diameter >= 4 cm)

trial_arms.intervention: Preoperative external beam RT + intracavitary brachytherapy followed by extrafascial hysterectomy
Preoperative RT + concurrent Cisplatin 40 mg/m2 weekly x 6 followed by extrafascial hysterectomy

key_passages.text: The addition of concurrent weekly cisplatin chemotherapy to radiotherapy significantly reduced the risk of recurrence and death in women with bulky stage IB cervical carcinoma.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Concurrent weekly cisplatin (40 mg/m2) with definitive pelvic radiation plus brachytherapy is the international standard of care for locally advanced cervical cancer.

entries.title: Adjuvant Chemotherapy following Chemoradiation as Primary Treatment for Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer (OUTBACK): An International, Open-Label, Randomised, Phase 3 Trial
entries.stage_criteria: Locally advanced cervical cancer (FIGO 2008 IB2, II, IIIB, IVA, or node-positive IB1/IIA)

trial_arms.intervention: Weekly Cisplatin 40 mg/m2 x 5 + pelvic RT (45-50.4 Gy) + image-guided brachytherapy
Standard CRT followed by 4 cycles of Carboplatin (AUC 5) + Paclitaxel (155 mg/m2 q3w)

key_passages.text: Adjuvant carboplatin and paclitaxel following standard chemoradiation did not improve progression-free or overall survival in women with locally advanced cervical cancer and resulted in substantially more toxic effects. Adjuvant chemotherapy should not be given.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Adjuvant chemotherapy after definitive chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced cervical cancer is not recommended and should be avoided.

entries.title: Adjuvant Chemoradiotherapy versus Radiotherapy Alone in Women with High-Risk Endometrial Cancer (PORTEC-3): Final Results of an International, Open-Label, Multicentre, Randomised, Phase 3 Trial
entries.stage_criteria: High-risk endometrial carcinoma: FIGO 2009 stage I grade 3 with deep myometrial invasion and/or LVSI, stage II, stage III, or serous/clear-cell histology

trial_arms.intervention: Pelvic RT 48.6 Gy in 27 fractions (1.8 Gy/fx)
Pelvic RT 48.6 Gy + 2 concurrent cycles Cisplatin 50 mg/m2 d1, 28 -> 4 adjuvant cycles Carboplatin AUC 5 + Paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 q3w

key_passages.text: Adjuvant chemoradiotherapy significantly improved overall survival and failure-free survival compared with radiotherapy alone for women with high-risk endometrial cancer, with the greatest benefit observed in women with stage III disease and serous histology.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Adjuvant chemoradiation (pelvic RT with concurrent cisplatin followed by carboplatin/paclitaxel) is the standard of care for high-risk and stage III endometrial cancer.

entries.title: Radiotherapy plus Concomitant and Adjuvant Temozolomide for Glioblastoma
entries.organization: EORTC Brain Tumour and Radiotherapy Groups / NCIC Clinical Trials Group
entries.stage_criteria: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (WHO grade 4), age 18-70 years, WHO performance status 0-2

trial_arms.intervention: Focal RT 60 Gy in 30 fractions (2.0 Gy/fx)
Focal RT 60 Gy + daily Temozolomide 75 mg/m2/day during RT -> 6 cycles adjuvant Temozolomide (150-200 mg/m2/day d1-5 q28d)

key_passages.text: The addition of temozolomide to radiotherapy for newly diagnosed glioblastoma resulted in a clinically meaningful and statistically significant survival benefit with minimal additional toxicity. Epigenetic silencing of the MGMT gene promoter was the strongest predictor of benefit.

entries.clinical_recommendation: The Stupp protocol (60 Gy in 30 fx with concurrent temozolomide 75 mg/m2 followed by 6 cycles of adjuvant temozolomide) is the global standard of care for glioblastoma.

entries.title: Chemoradiotherapy for Subtotally Resected Low-Grade Glioma
entries.stage_criteria: High-risk grade 2 astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma, or oligoastrocytoma (age >= 40 with any resection, or age < 40 with subtotal resection or biopsy)

trial_arms.intervention: Focal RT 54 Gy in 30 fractions (1.8 Gy/fx)
Focal RT 54 Gy followed by 6 cycles of PCV (Procarbazine, CCNU, Vincristine)

key_passages.text: In patients with high-risk low-grade glioma, the addition of six cycles of PCV chemotherapy to radiotherapy was associated with significantly longer progression-free survival and overall survival than radiotherapy alone.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Radiotherapy (54 Gy) followed by PCV (or temozolomide) chemotherapy is the standard of care for adults with high-risk grade 2 gliomas.

entries.title: Effect of Axillary Dissection vs No Axillary Dissection on 10-Year Overall Survival Among Women With Invasive Breast Cancer and Sentinel Node Metastases: The ACOSOG Z0011 (Alliance) Randomized Clinical Trial
entries.stage_criteria: Clinical T1-T2 N0 breast cancer with 1 to 2 sentinel lymph nodes containing metastases undergoing breast-conserving therapy and whole-breast irradiation

trial_arms.intervention: Complete level I and II axillary lymph node dissection
No further axillary dissection

endpoints.lymphedema_and_morbidity: Significantly lower wound infections, paresthesias, and lymphedema in SLNB-alone arm

key_passages.text: Among women with T1 or T2 invasive breast cancer, no palpable axillary adenopathy, and 1 or 2 sentinel lymph nodes containing metastases, 10-year overall survival and regional recurrence did not differ significantly between SLNB alone and completion ALND when treated with breast-conserving surgery and whole-breast irradiation.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Completion axillary lymph node dissection may be safely omitted in patients with cT1-2N0 breast cancer and 1-2 positive sentinel nodes treated with lumpectomy and whole-breast radiation.

entries.title: Adjuvant Capecitabine for Breast Cancer after Preoperative Chemotherapy
entries.stage_criteria: HER2-negative breast cancer with pathologically confirmed residual invasive disease in breast or axilla after neoadjuvant anthracycline/taxane chemotherapy

trial_arms.intervention: Standard post-surgery therapy
Capecitabine 1250 mg/m2 PO bid on days 1-14 every 21 days for 6-8 cycles

key_passages.text: Among patients with HER2-negative breast cancer who had residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, the addition of adjuvant capecitabine therapy was safe and effective in prolonging disease-free and overall survival, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Adjuvant Capecitabine (1250 mg/m2 PO bid d1-14 q3w for 6-8 cycles) is Category 1 standard of care for triple-negative breast cancer with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

entries.title: Trastuzumab Emtansine for Residual Invasive HER2-Positive Breast Cancer
entries.stage_criteria: HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive disease in breast or axilla after preoperative chemotherapy plus HER2-targeted therapy

trial_arms.intervention: Trastuzumab 6 mg/kg IV q3w for 14 cycles
Trastuzumab Emtansine 3.6 mg/kg IV q3w for 14 cycles (42 weeks)

key_passages.text: The risk of recurrence of invasive breast cancer or death was 50% lower with adjuvant T-DM1 than with trastuzumab alone in patients with HER2-positive early breast cancer who had residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy.

entries.clinical_recommendation: Adjuvant Trastuzumab Emtansine (T-DM1, 3.6 mg/kg q3w for 14 cycles) is the Category 1 standard of care for HER2-positive breast cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant taxane/trastuzumab therapy.

trials.title: Concurrent Chemotherapy and Radiotherapy for Organ Preservation in Advanced Laryngeal Cancer
trials.organization: Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (RTOG) / NRG Oncology
trials.stage_criteria: Stage III or IV nonmetastatic squamous cell carcinoma of glottic or supraglottic larynx requiring total laryngectomy (T2-T4, N0-N3, M0; excluding T1 and T4 with extensive cartilage invasion)

trial_arms.intervention: Definitive RT 70 Gy in 35 daily fractions (2.0 Gy/fx) with concurrent Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 22, and 43
Induction Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 + 5-FU 1000 mg/m2/day continuous infusion d1-5 x 3 cycles followed by definitive RT 70 Gy
Definitive RT 70 Gy in 35 daily fractions (2.0 Gy/fx)

key_passages.text: Concurrent cisplatin and radiotherapy provides superior locoregional control and larynx preservation compared with induction chemotherapy followed by radiation or radiation alone. Long-term overall survival did not differ significantly between arms.

Concurrent chemoradiotherapy was associated with a relative risk reduction of locoregional failure of 42% compared with RT alone (HR 0.58, p=0.0015) and 34% compared with induction chemotherapy (HR 0.66, p=0.0037).

trials.clinical_recommendation: Concurrent high-dose cisplatin (100 mg/m2 q3w) with definitive radiation (70 Gy) is the standard nonsurgical organ preservation strategy for locally advanced laryngeal cancer.

trials.title: Postoperative Concurrent Chemotherapy and Radiotherapy for High-Risk Squamous-Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck
trials.organization: European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC)
trials.stage_criteria: Resected stage III-IV squamous-cell carcinoma of oral cavity, oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx with high-risk features (positive surgical margins, extranodal extension, pT3-T4, vascular/perineural invasion, or level IV/V nodal involvement)

trial_arms.intervention: Postoperative RT 66 Gy in 33 fractions (2.0 Gy/fx) with concurrent Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 22, and 43
Postoperative RT 66 Gy in 33 fractions (2.0 Gy/fx)

key_passages.text: Postoperative concurrent administration of cisplatin with radiotherapy resulted in significant improvements in progression-free survival (HR 0.75, p=0.04), overall survival (HR 0.70, p=0.02), and locoregional control (HR 0.57, p=0.007) compared with radiotherapy alone in high-risk head and neck cancer.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Postoperative concurrent cisplatin (100 mg/m2 q3w x 3 cycles) plus 66 Gy radiation is standard for resected head and neck cancer with positive margins or extranodal nodal extension.

trials.title: Postoperative Concurrent Radiotherapy and Chemotherapy for High-Risk Squamous-Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck
trials.stage_criteria: Resected stage III-IV squamous-cell carcinoma of oral cavity, oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx with >=2 involved regional lymph nodes, extracapsular extension (ENE), or microscopically positive surgical margins

trial_arms.intervention: Postoperative RT 60-66 Gy in 30-33 fractions + concurrent Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 22, and 43
Postoperative RT 60-66 Gy in 30-33 fractions

key_passages.text: Concurrent postoperative radiotherapy and cisplatin significantly improved locoregional control (HR 0.61, p=0.01) and disease-free survival (HR 0.78, p=0.04) among high-risk patients with resected head and neck cancer.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Adjuvant cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy significantly reduces locoregional failure in surgically resected HNSCC harboring positive margins or extracapsular nodal spread.

trials.title: Defining Risk Levels in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Cancers: A Comparative Analysis of Concurrent Postoperative Radiation Plus Chemotherapy Trials of the EORTC (#22931) and RTOG (#9501)
trials.stage_criteria: Pooled patient-level data from 792 patients enrolled in EORTC 22931 and RTOG 9501

key_passages.text: Definitive benefit of postoperative concurrent cisplatin and RT is restricted to patients with microscopically positive surgical margins and/or extracapsular extension (ECE/ENE). Patients with multiple involved nodes without ECE did not demonstrate an overall survival benefit from adding chemotherapy.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Microscopically positive surgical margins and extranodal nodal extension are the absolute standard indications for adjuvant concurrent chemoradiation; patients with other intermediate features (T3-4, multiple nodes without ENE) may receive RT alone.

trials.title: Randomized Phase III Trial of Concurrent Accelerated Radiation Plus Cisplatin With or Without Cetuximab for Stage III to IV Head and Neck Carcinoma
trials.organization: Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (RTOG) / NRG Oncology
trials.stage_criteria: Nonmetastatic stage III/IV squamous cell carcinoma of oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx

trial_arms.intervention: Accelerated RT (72 Gy in 42 fractions over 6 weeks) + Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV d1, 22
Accelerated RT + Cisplatin + Cetuximab (400 mg/m2 loading, then 250 mg/m2 weekly)

endpoints.grade_3_4_adverse_events: Significantly higher mucositis and radiation dermatitis in cetuximab arm

key_passages.text: The addition of cetuximab to cisplatin-based concurrent accelerated radiation therapy failed to improve progression-free survival or overall survival and resulted in more frequent interruptions in radiation therapy and worse acute toxic effects. Cisplatin + RT remains standard.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Cetuximab should not be added to standard concurrent cisplatin-radiotherapy in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

trials.title: Radiotherapy with or without Cetuximab in the Treatment of Locoregionally Advanced Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck
trials.stage_criteria: Locoregionally advanced Stage III-IV squamous cell carcinoma of oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx

trial_arms.intervention: Definitive RT (70 Gy) + Cetuximab (400 mg/m2 load then 250 mg/m2 weekly)
Definitive RT alone (70 Gy)

key_passages.text: Definitive radiotherapy plus cetuximab significantly improves locoregional control and overall survival compared with radiotherapy alone in locoregionally advanced head and neck cancer, without exacerbating common radiation-related mucositis.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Cetuximab + definitive RT is a Category 1 alternative for patients with locally advanced HNSCC who are medically unfit for cisplatin (e.g. renal failure, pre-existing neuropathy, severe hearing loss).

trials.title: Radiotherapy plus Cetuximab or Cisplatin in Human Papillomavirus-Positive Oropharyngeal Cancer: A Randomised, Multicentre, Non-Inferiority Trial
trials.stage_criteria: Locally advanced HPV/p16-positive squamous cell carcinoma of oropharynx (T1-T2 N2a-N3 or T3-T4 N0-N3, AJCC 7th)

trial_arms.intervention: Accelerated IMRT 70 Gy in 35 fx / 6 wks + Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 d1, 22
Accelerated IMRT 70 Gy in 35 fx / 6 wks + Cetuximab loading and weekly

key_passages.text: For patients with HPV-positive oropharyngeal carcinoma, radiotherapy plus cetuximab showed inferior overall survival and progression-free survival compared with radiotherapy plus cisplatin, with similar rates of overall acute and late toxicity. Radiotherapy plus cisplatin remains the standard of care.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Cisplatin concurrent with definitive radiotherapy remains the non-negotiable standard of care for HPV-positive oropharynx cancer; cetuximab de-intensification is inferior and not guideline concordant.

trials.title: Durvalumab after Chemoradiotherapy in Stage III Non–Small-Cell Lung Cancer
trials.stage_criteria: Unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer with no progression after definitive concurrent platinum-based chemoradiotherapy (minimum RT dose 54-66 Gy)

trial_arms.intervention: Durvalumab 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks for up to 12 months
Placebo every 2 weeks for up to 12 months

key_passages.text: Consolidation durvalumab significantly prolonged progression-free survival and overall survival compared with placebo in patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC who did not have disease progression after concurrent chemoradiotherapy, with manageable safety profile.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Durvalumab consolidation (10 mg/kg q2w or 1500 mg q4w x 12 months) is Category 1 standard of care following definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy in non-progressing unresectable stage III NSCLC.

trials.title: High-Dose Radiotherapy with or without Cetuximab for Patients with Inoperable Stage III Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer: A Multicentre, Randomised, Open-Label Phase 3 Study
trials.organization: Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (RTOG) / NRG Oncology
trials.stage_criteria: Inoperable stage III non-small cell lung cancer, ECOG 0-1, FEV1 >= 1.2 L or >= 50% predicted

trial_arms.intervention: 60 Gy in 30 daily fractions + concurrent carboplatin/paclitaxel +/- cetuximab
74 Gy in 37 daily fractions + concurrent carboplatin/paclitaxel +/- cetuximab

endpoints.multivariate_predictors_of_death: High-dose radiation arm (HR 1.35) and heart V40/V5/V30 dose volume parameters

key_passages.text: 74 Gy radiation dose escalation was harmful compared with standard-dose 60 Gy thoracic radiotherapy in stage III NSCLC. Excess mortality was strongly correlated with cardiac radiation exposure. Standard 60 Gy in 30 fractions remains the definitive standard.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Definitive radiation prescription for stage III NSCLC must not exceed 60-66 Gy in standard 2 Gy fractions; strict cardiac sparing (mean heart dose, V30, V5) is essential.

trials.title: Concurrent Once-Daily versus Twice-Daily Chemoradiotherapy in Patients with Limited-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer
trials.organization: CONVERT Study Team / Cancer Research UK
trials.stage_criteria: Limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC), ECOG performance status 0-1, normal organ function

trial_arms.intervention: 45 Gy in 30 fractions (1.5 Gy bid over 3 weeks) + concurrent cisplatin/etoposide
66 Gy in 33 fractions (2.0 Gy qd over 6.5 weeks) + concurrent cisplatin/etoposide

key_passages.text: Survival outcomes and toxicity were similar between twice-daily 45 Gy and once-daily 66 Gy chemoradiotherapy. Twice-daily 45 Gy in 3 weeks remains the standard international benchmark, with once-daily 66 Gy offering a safe and valid alternative.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Accelerated twice-daily thoracic radiotherapy (45 Gy in 30 fx bid over 3 weeks) starting with Cycle 1-2 of cisplatin/etoposide is standard for limited-stage SCLC.

trials.title: Radiotherapy to the Primary Tumour for Newly Diagnosed, Metastatic Prostate Cancer (STAMPEDE): A Randomised Controlled Phase 3 Trial
trials.organization: MRC Clinical Trials Unit / STAMPEDE Investigators
trials.stage_criteria: Newly diagnosed metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC / mCSPC)

trial_arms.intervention: Lifelong ADT +/- early Docetaxel
Standard systemic therapy + Prostate RT (55 Gy / 20 fx daily over 4 weeks or 36 Gy / 6 fx weekly over 6 weeks)

key_passages.text: Prostate radiotherapy improved overall survival in men with newly diagnosed metastatic prostate cancer who had low metastatic burden (CHAARTED criteria: <4 bone metastases and no visceral metastases). Primary prostate RT should be recommended for low-volume mHSPC.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Prostate-directed external beam radiotherapy (55 Gy / 20 fx or 36 Gy / 6 fx) is standard Category 1 therapy for men with newly diagnosed low-volume metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer.

trials.title: Radiotherapy with or without Short-Term Androgen Deprivation for Localized Prostate Cancer
trials.stage_criteria: Localized adenocarcinoma of the prostate (T1b-T2b, PSA <= 20 ng/mL, Gleason score <= 7)

trial_arms.intervention: Definitive RT 66.6 Gy
Definitive RT 66.6 Gy + 4 months of ADT (Flutamide + Goserelin starting 2 months prior to RT)

endpoints.subgroup_benefit: Benefit concentrated entirely in intermediate-risk disease; low-risk patients showed no OS improvement (p=0.48)

key_passages.text: The addition of 4 months of short-term androgen-deprivation therapy to radiotherapy significantly improved overall survival and decreased disease-specific mortality for men with intermediate-risk localized prostate cancer.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Short-term androgen deprivation therapy (4 to 6 months) combined with definitive radiation therapy is Category 1 standard for intermediate-risk prostate cancer.

trials.title: Duration of Androgen Suppression in the Treatment of Locally Advanced Prostate Cancer
trials.organization: European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC)
trials.stage_criteria: Locally advanced / high-risk localized prostate cancer (T1c-T2b N0 with PSA >= 3x ULN or Gleason >= 8, or T3-T4 N0-N1)

trial_arms.intervention: External beam RT (70 Gy) + 6 months LHRH agonist
External beam RT (70 Gy) + 36 months LHRH agonist

key_passages.text: The combination of radiotherapy plus 6 months of androgen suppression provides inferior overall survival compared with radiotherapy plus 3 years of androgen suppression in locally advanced and high-risk prostate cancer.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Long-term androgen deprivation therapy (24-36 months) in combination with high-dose definitive radiotherapy is the established standard for high-risk and very high-risk localized prostate cancer.

trials.title: Radiotherapy with or without Chemotherapy in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer
trials.organization: BC2001 Trial Investigators / Cancer Research UK
trials.stage_criteria: Muscle-invasive adenocarcinoma or urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder (T2-T4a N0 M0)

trial_arms.intervention: Definitive pelvic RT (55 Gy / 20 fx or 64 Gy / 32 fx)
Definitive pelvic RT + 5-FU (500 mg/m2/d d1-5 & d16-20) + Mitomycin C (12 mg/m2 d1)

endpoints.salvage_cystectomy_rate: Significantly reduced with CRT without increased late toxic effects

key_passages.text: Synchronous chemotherapy with fluorouracil and mitomycin C during definitive radiotherapy significantly improved locoregional disease-free survival and reduced cystectomy rates without increasing late grade 3 or 4 adverse events.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Concurrent 5-FU and Mitomycin C with definitive radiotherapy is the Category 1 standard regimen for trimodality bladder-preserving therapy in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

trials.title: Preoperative Chemoradiotherapy for Esophageal or Junctional Cancer
trials.stage_criteria: Resectable esophageal or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, or large-cell carcinoma (cT1N1 or cT2-3N0-1, M0)

trial_arms.intervention: Transthoracic or transhiatal esophagectomy with lymphadenectomy
Weekly Paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 + Carboplatin AUC 2 for 5 weeks with concurrent RT 41.4 Gy (23 fx of 1.8 Gy) followed by surgery

key_passages.text: Preoperative chemoradiotherapy with weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel combined with 41.4 Gy radiation significantly improved overall survival compared with surgery alone in patients with resectable esophageal or GEJ cancer.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy using the CROSS regimen (weekly carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 with 41.4 Gy RT) is a standard Category 1 trimodality approach for resectable esophageal and GEJ cancers.

trials.title: Adjuvant Nivolumab in Resected Esophageal or Gastroesophageal Junction Cancer
trials.stage_criteria: Resected stage II or III esophageal or gastroesophageal junction cancer with residual pathologic disease (>= ypT1 or ypN+) after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and R0 surgical resection

trial_arms.intervention: Nivolumab 240 mg IV q2w for 16 weeks, then 480 mg q4w up to total 1 year
Placebo for up to total 1 year

key_passages.text: Among patients with resected esophageal or GE junction cancer who had received neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and had residual pathologic disease, disease-free survival was significantly doubled with adjuvant nivolumab compared with placebo.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Adjuvant Nivolumab for 1 year is Category 1 standard for patients with residual pathologic disease (non-pCR) following neoadjuvant chemoradiation and complete resection.

trials.title: Short-Course Radiotherapy Followed by Chemotherapy before Total Mesorectal Excision (TME) versus Preoperative Chemoradiotherapy, TME, and Optional Adjuvant Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (RAPIDO): A Randomised, Open-Label, Phase 3 Trial
trials.stage_criteria: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma with high-risk features on pelvic MRI: cT4a/b, extramural venous invasion (EMVI+), cN2, involved mesorectal fascia (MRF+), or enlarged lateral lymph nodes

trial_arms.intervention: Short-course RT (5 x 5 Gy = 25 Gy in 1 week) -> 6 cycles CAPOX or 9 cycles FOLFOX4 consolidation chemotherapy -> TME surgery
Long-course CRT (50-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fx + Capecitabine) -> TME surgery -> optional adjuvant CAPOX/FOLFOX

key_passages.text: Total neoadjuvant therapy with short-course radiotherapy followed by consolidation chemotherapy before TME significantly reduced the probability of disease-related treatment failure and distant metastasis and doubled the pathological complete response rate compared with standard chemoradiotherapy.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Total Neoadjuvant Therapy (TNT) using short-course RT (5x5 Gy) followed by consolidation CAPOX/FOLFOX is Category 1 standard for MRI-defined high-risk locally advanced rectal cancer.

trials.title: Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy with FOLFIRINOX and Preoperative Chemoradiotherapy for Patients with Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (UNICANCER-PRODIGE 23): A Multicentre, Randomised, Open-Label, Phase 3 Trial
trials.stage_criteria: Locally advanced rectal cancer (cT3 or cT4, M0)

trial_arms.intervention: 6 cycles mFOLFIRINOX induction -> Preoperative CRT (50 Gy + Capecitabine) -> TME surgery -> 3 months adjuvant mFOLFOX6
Preoperative CRT (50 Gy + Capecitabine) -> TME surgery -> 6 months adjuvant mFOLFOX6

key_passages.text: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with mFOLFIRINOX before preoperative chemoradiotherapy significantly improved disease-free survival, metastasis-free survival, and pathological complete response rate compared with standard preoperative chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Induction mFOLFIRINOX followed by preoperative chemoradiotherapy is a Category 1 TNT regimen for fit patients with locally advanced rectal cancer.

trials.title: Chemoradiation with or without Maintenance Chemotherapy for Anal Cancer (ACT II): A Randomised, Factorial, Phase 3 Trial
trials.organization: UK NCRI Anal Cancer Sub-Group / ACT II
trials.stage_criteria: Epidermoid anal canal carcinoma (any stage without distant metastasis)

trial_arms.intervention: RT 50.4 Gy + 5-FU 1000 mg/m2/d d1-4 & d29-32 + Mitomycin C 12 mg/m2 d1
RT 50.4 Gy + 5-FU 1000 mg/m2/d d1-4 & d29-32 + Cisplatin 60 mg/m2 d1, 29

endpoints.maintenance_chemotherapy_effect: No benefit in PFS (HR 0.95, p=0.70) or OS (HR 0.86, p=0.37); caused added toxicity

key_passages.text: Mitomycin C and Cisplatin produced equivalent response rates and progression-free survival, but Cisplatin caused higher hematologic toxicity. Maintenance chemotherapy provided no clinical benefit. 5-FU and Mitomycin C concurrent with radiotherapy remains the definitive standard of care.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Definitive chemoradiation with 5-FU and Mitomycin C is the standard of care for epidermoid anal cancer; maintenance chemotherapy should not be administered.

trials.title: FOLFIRINOX or Gemcitabine as Adjuvant Therapy for Pancreatic Cancer
trials.stage_criteria: Completely resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (R0 or R1 resection), ECOG performance status 0-1, postoperative CA19-9 < 180 U/mL

trial_arms.intervention: Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, Leucovorin 400 mg/m2, Irinotecan 180 or 150 mg/m2, 5-FU continuous 2400 mg/m2 over 46h q2w for 24 weeks (12 cycles)
Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, 15 q28d for 6 cycles

key_passages.text: Adjuvant therapy with a modified FOLFIRINOX regimen led to significantly longer overall survival and disease-free survival than gemcitabine among patients with resected pancreatic cancer.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Modified FOLFIRINOX is the Category 1 standard adjuvant chemotherapy for fit patients (ECOG 0-1, preserved organ function) following resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

trials.title: Cisplatin, Radiation, and Adjuvant Hysterectomy for Bulky Stage IB Cervical Carcinoma
trials.stage_criteria: Bulky stage IB carcinoma of the cervix (tumor diameter >= 4 cm)

trial_arms.intervention: Preoperative external beam RT + intracavitary brachytherapy followed by extrafascial hysterectomy
Preoperative RT + concurrent Cisplatin 40 mg/m2 weekly x 6 followed by extrafascial hysterectomy

key_passages.text: The addition of concurrent weekly cisplatin chemotherapy to radiotherapy significantly reduced the risk of recurrence and death in women with bulky stage IB cervical carcinoma.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Concurrent weekly cisplatin (40 mg/m2) with definitive pelvic radiation plus brachytherapy is the international standard of care for locally advanced cervical cancer.

trials.title: Adjuvant Chemotherapy following Chemoradiation as Primary Treatment for Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer (OUTBACK): An International, Open-Label, Randomised, Phase 3 Trial
trials.stage_criteria: Locally advanced cervical cancer (FIGO 2008 IB2, II, IIIB, IVA, or node-positive IB1/IIA)

trial_arms.intervention: Weekly Cisplatin 40 mg/m2 x 5 + pelvic RT (45-50.4 Gy) + image-guided brachytherapy
Standard CRT followed by 4 cycles of Carboplatin (AUC 5) + Paclitaxel (155 mg/m2 q3w)

key_passages.text: Adjuvant carboplatin and paclitaxel following standard chemoradiation did not improve progression-free or overall survival in women with locally advanced cervical cancer and resulted in substantially more toxic effects. Adjuvant chemotherapy should not be given.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Adjuvant chemotherapy after definitive chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced cervical cancer is not recommended and should be avoided.

trials.title: Adjuvant Chemoradiotherapy versus Radiotherapy Alone in Women with High-Risk Endometrial Cancer (PORTEC-3): Final Results of an International, Open-Label, Multicentre, Randomised, Phase 3 Trial
trials.stage_criteria: High-risk endometrial carcinoma: FIGO 2009 stage I grade 3 with deep myometrial invasion and/or LVSI, stage II, stage III, or serous/clear-cell histology

trial_arms.intervention: Pelvic RT 48.6 Gy in 27 fractions (1.8 Gy/fx)
Pelvic RT 48.6 Gy + 2 concurrent cycles Cisplatin 50 mg/m2 d1, 28 -> 4 adjuvant cycles Carboplatin AUC 5 + Paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 q3w

key_passages.text: Adjuvant chemoradiotherapy significantly improved overall survival and failure-free survival compared with radiotherapy alone for women with high-risk endometrial cancer, with the greatest benefit observed in women with stage III disease and serous histology.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Adjuvant chemoradiation (pelvic RT with concurrent cisplatin followed by carboplatin/paclitaxel) is the standard of care for high-risk and stage III endometrial cancer.

trials.title: Radiotherapy plus Concomitant and Adjuvant Temozolomide for Glioblastoma
trials.organization: EORTC Brain Tumour and Radiotherapy Groups / NCIC Clinical Trials Group
trials.stage_criteria: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (WHO grade 4), age 18-70 years, WHO performance status 0-2

trial_arms.intervention: Focal RT 60 Gy in 30 fractions (2.0 Gy/fx)
Focal RT 60 Gy + daily Temozolomide 75 mg/m2/day during RT -> 6 cycles adjuvant Temozolomide (150-200 mg/m2/day d1-5 q28d)

key_passages.text: The addition of temozolomide to radiotherapy for newly diagnosed glioblastoma resulted in a clinically meaningful and statistically significant survival benefit with minimal additional toxicity. Epigenetic silencing of the MGMT gene promoter was the strongest predictor of benefit.

trials.clinical_recommendation: The Stupp protocol (60 Gy in 30 fx with concurrent temozolomide 75 mg/m2 followed by 6 cycles of adjuvant temozolomide) is the global standard of care for glioblastoma.

trials.title: Chemoradiotherapy for Subtotally Resected Low-Grade Glioma
trials.stage_criteria: High-risk grade 2 astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma, or oligoastrocytoma (age >= 40 with any resection, or age < 40 with subtotal resection or biopsy)

trial_arms.intervention: Focal RT 54 Gy in 30 fractions (1.8 Gy/fx)
Focal RT 54 Gy followed by 6 cycles of PCV (Procarbazine, CCNU, Vincristine)

key_passages.text: In patients with high-risk low-grade glioma, the addition of six cycles of PCV chemotherapy to radiotherapy was associated with significantly longer progression-free survival and overall survival than radiotherapy alone.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Radiotherapy (54 Gy) followed by PCV (or temozolomide) chemotherapy is the standard of care for adults with high-risk grade 2 gliomas.

trials.title: Effect of Axillary Dissection vs No Axillary Dissection on 10-Year Overall Survival Among Women With Invasive Breast Cancer and Sentinel Node Metastases: The ACOSOG Z0011 (Alliance) Randomized Clinical Trial
trials.stage_criteria: Clinical T1-T2 N0 breast cancer with 1 to 2 sentinel lymph nodes containing metastases undergoing breast-conserving therapy and whole-breast irradiation

trial_arms.intervention: Complete level I and II axillary lymph node dissection
No further axillary dissection

endpoints.lymphedema_and_morbidity: Significantly lower wound infections, paresthesias, and lymphedema in SLNB-alone arm

key_passages.text: Among women with T1 or T2 invasive breast cancer, no palpable axillary adenopathy, and 1 or 2 sentinel lymph nodes containing metastases, 10-year overall survival and regional recurrence did not differ significantly between SLNB alone and completion ALND when treated with breast-conserving surgery and whole-breast irradiation.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Completion axillary lymph node dissection may be safely omitted in patients with cT1-2N0 breast cancer and 1-2 positive sentinel nodes treated with lumpectomy and whole-breast radiation.

trials.title: Adjuvant Capecitabine for Breast Cancer after Preoperative Chemotherapy
trials.stage_criteria: HER2-negative breast cancer with pathologically confirmed residual invasive disease in breast or axilla after neoadjuvant anthracycline/taxane chemotherapy

trial_arms.intervention: Standard post-surgery therapy
Capecitabine 1250 mg/m2 PO bid on days 1-14 every 21 days for 6-8 cycles

key_passages.text: Among patients with HER2-negative breast cancer who had residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, the addition of adjuvant capecitabine therapy was safe and effective in prolonging disease-free and overall survival, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Adjuvant Capecitabine (1250 mg/m2 PO bid d1-14 q3w for 6-8 cycles) is Category 1 standard of care for triple-negative breast cancer with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

trials.title: Trastuzumab Emtansine for Residual Invasive HER2-Positive Breast Cancer
trials.stage_criteria: HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive disease in breast or axilla after preoperative chemotherapy plus HER2-targeted therapy

trial_arms.intervention: Trastuzumab 6 mg/kg IV q3w for 14 cycles
Trastuzumab Emtansine 3.6 mg/kg IV q3w for 14 cycles (42 weeks)

key_passages.text: The risk of recurrence of invasive breast cancer or death was 50% lower with adjuvant T-DM1 than with trastuzumab alone in patients with HER2-positive early breast cancer who had residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy.

trials.clinical_recommendation: Adjuvant Trastuzumab Emtansine (T-DM1, 3.6 mg/kg q3w for 14 cycles) is the Category 1 standard of care for HER2-positive breast cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant taxane/trastuzumab therapy.
